name: CapaAviso
author: carlesgarciamaestre

sections.description:
CapaAviso displays notices, announcements and alerts on your website using overlay layers inside the page itself, instead of traditional pop-up windows. Since it never uses window.open, no pop-up blocker can block them.

The name CapaAviso is a coined Spanish word: «capa» (overlay layer) + «aviso» (notice).

The plugin interface is currently in Spanish; translations can be contributed via translate.wordpress.org.

Features

  • Master switch: enable or disable all notices from the settings page, without deactivating the plugin.
  • Multiple parallel notices: create as many as you need, each with its own configuration.
  • Scope per notice: whole site, home page only, only on site entry (first page of the visit), or only via shortcode [capav_aviso id="123"].
  • 5 ready-made templates (text-only, image-only, mixed with button & document, semi-transparent layer, multi-page with navigation) — self-contained with inline styles, so they look the same with any theme. Sample images are bundled, so they work out of the box.
  • One-click example notices: create all 5 templates as deactivated notices from the Settings page — existing notices are never touched.
  • One-click actions in the notice list: activate/deactivate without editing, and duplicate a notice (the copy starts as a deactivated draft).
  • Built-in instructions page inside the WordPress admin.
  • For each notice you can define:
    • Ordinal (display order when several notices are active).
    • Internal name (only visible in the back-end).
    • Full HTML content with a visual editor (Design) or code editor (HTML).
    • Attached images and documents uploaded from the media library and inserted into the content.
    • Dimensions in %, px, vw/vh, with optional automatic height.
    • Position: centered, top, bottom, left, right and the four corners.
    • Display time with configurable auto-close (seconds).
    • Manual close with an × button (and the Escape key).
    • Sound alert on open (upload your own mp3/ogg).
    • Background color with a visual color picker, plus a transparent background option (no color, no shadow) for glass-panel effects.
    • Expiration date: the notice switches itself off when the date is reached (site local time).
    • “Do not show again” link: visitors who click it will not see that notice again in their browser for 1 year (localStorage + cookie, no IPs stored).
  • Notice list with status, position, scope, dimensions and ordinal columns.
  • Lightweight: own CSS and JS, no external dependencies.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the capaviso folder to /wp-content/plugins/ (or install the ZIP from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin).
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins menu.
  3. You will see the Avisos emergentes menu in the admin panel.
  4. Create and enable notices; the master switch is under Avisos emergentes > Ajustes.
sections.faq:
Why can’t pop-up blockers block it?

Because it does not open new windows: it draws a layer (fixed div) over the page, just like a modal. Blockers only intercept window.open.

Can I switch off all notices without deactivating the plugin?

Yes: in Avisos emergentes > Ajustes uncheck the master switch.

Does the sound always play?

Modern browsers may block automatic audio until the user interacts with the page; that is a browser restriction, not a plugin limitation.
sections.changelog:
2.0.1

  • Fixed: on sites coming from “Aviso Emergente” 1.x, legacy settings (master switch, z-index) are now migrated before default options are created on activation, so they are no longer overwritten.

2.0.0

  • The plugin is now called CapaAviso (formerly “Aviso Emergente”). CapaAviso is a coined Spanish word: «capa» (layer) + «aviso» (notice) — overlay notices.
  • All identifiers are now prefixed with capav_ (functions, classes, options, post meta, shortcode, AJAX actions, script/style handles) to avoid any naming collision.
  • The shortcode is now [capav_aviso id="123"] (formerly [ae_aviso]). If you used the old shortcode in any page, please update it.
  • Existing notices, settings and metadata are migrated automatically on update — nothing is lost.
  • Security hardening: notice content is now filtered through an allowlist (wp_kses with the post tags plus <button>) before output.

1.3.2

  • New: the built-in instructions page now includes annotated screenshots of every screen and two published example notices.

1.3.1

  • Improved: the activate/deactivate control in the notice list is now a visual switch (green = active, red = inactive).

1.3.0

  • New: “Transparent background” option per notice (no color, no shadow) for glass-panel effects.
  • New: templates now ship with bundled sample images — they work out of the box, nothing to upload.
  • New: one-click button in Settings creates the 5 example notices (deactivated) in the list, never replacing existing notices.

1.2.0

  • New: scope per notice — whole site, home page only, only on site entry (first page of the visit), or only via shortcode [capav_aviso id="123"].
  • New: 5 ready-made templates (text-only, image-only, mixed with button & document, semi-transparent layer, multi-page with navigation), self-contained so they survive any theme.
  • New: activate/deactivate a notice with one click from the notice list (no need to edit it).
  • New: duplicate a notice from the list (the copy starts as a deactivated draft).
  • New: built-in instructions page inside the WordPress admin.

1.1.0

  • New: per-notice expiration date (switches off automatically when the date is reached, in site local time).
  • New: “Do not show again” option per notice; visitors who click it will not see that notice again in their browser for 1 year (localStorage + cookie, no IPs stored).

1.0.1

  • Fixed: the z-index is now applied to the whole overlay layer, preventing themes with stacking contexts (WPBakery, sliders, fixed headers) from covering the notices.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
